system.name: FleetIO
system.one_liner: a learning-based storage virtualization framework that uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to balance performance isolation and utilization for shared SSDs

components.name: Workload
components.role: application workload generating I/O to a vSSD

components.name: vSSD-1
components.role: virtual SSD instance hosting its own RL agent

components.name: RL Agent
components.role: monitors the vSSD's I/O traffic, extracts storage states, and selects the RL action with the highest predicted reward

components.name: Monitor
components.role: tracks storage states such as I/O latency, throughput, and queue delay

components.name: RL Model
components.role: predicts the highest-reward RL action (e.g. Harvest, Make_Harvestable) from RL states

components.name: Admission Control
components.role: validates and filters RL agents' actions, batching and reordering them before they run on the shared SSD

components.name: SSD Virtualization
components.role: platform on which admitted actions are executed on the shared SSD

components.name: vSSD Manager
components.role: manages vSSD resources within SSD virtualization

components.name: Ghost Superblock Manager
components.role: manages harvestable storage tracked as ghost superblocks

components.name: ghost Superblock
components.role: harvestable storage unit tracked by the Ghost Superblock Manager

content.key_idea: Per-vSSD RL agents independently choose harvest/allocation actions from monitored I/O states; a shared admission-control stage validates, batches, and reorders these actions before they reach the SSD.
content.reading_order: Top row: three workloads each drive a vSSD's RL agent (monitor plus model). Their actions and rewards flow down through admission control into SSD virtualization's managers.

evidence: We show the system architecture of FleetIO in Figure 5.
FleetIO deploys an RL agent in each vSSD, enabling scalability to support multiple vSSDs.
we design an admission control mechanism (Figure 5) that ingests each RL agent's Harvest() and Make_Harvestable() actions

summary: This figure shows FleetIO's overall system architecture. FleetIO deploys an independent RL agent inside each vSSD so the design scales to many virtual SSDs. Three identical vSSD columns are shown, each with a Monitor sub-module that extracts I/O latency, throughput, and queue-delay states from the workload, and an RL Model that selects the action predicted to earn the highest reward; each agent exchanges Actions and Reward signals with a shared Admission Control stage below. Admission Control filters out inadmissible actions (letting cloud providers customize permission checks per vSSD), and processes the remaining Harvest()/Make_Harvestable() actions in batches, reordering each batch so harvestable-resource-producing actions run before consuming ones. The admitted actions are submitted to the SSD Virtualization layer, which contains a vSSD Manager and a Ghost Superblock Manager that tracks harvestable storage as ghost superblocks.
